alert_summary: PowerShell was launched with an encoded command from wscript.exe to download and execute code from external IP 45.146.164.110:8080/u. The activity shows obfuscated PowerShell execution initiated by a script downloaded to the user profile, with 55 matching events indicating repeated behavior.

risk_assessment.rationale: The parent process wscript.exe executing PowerShell with -Enc indicates deliberate obfuscation consistent with T1027 and PowerShell execution via T1059.001. The decoded command uses Net.WebClient to pull a script from an external server, which is typical for payload retrieval and post-compromise activity. The high evidence count of 55 suggests repeated or reconnaissance-style execution rather than a one-off anomaly. Combined with an unknown external IP and an untrusted script path under the user Downloads folder, this represents high-severity, high-confidence malicious behavior.

recommended_actions: Escalate to a human analyst for manual review
recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Isolate the host dev-klyam01.victimcorp.com and capture a full memory dump before shutdown to preserve in-memory PowerShell artifacts and any injected threads.
Block outbound connections to 45.146.164.110:8080 at perimeter and internal egress controls, and hunt for other hosts contacting the same IP or URL path /u.
Collect and review the file C:\Users\ke.li.yam\Downloads\build-helper.js, its creation/modification times, and any parent process that wrote it, plus user ke.li.yam activity and recent logon events.

Search Sysmon and PowerShell logs across the environment for additional wscript.exe -> powershell.exe -Enc executions, especially with similar encoded payloads or WebClient downloads, to scope lateral movement.
triage_rationale_experimental: PowerShell was launched with an encoded command from wscript.exe to download and execute code from an external IP, matching obfuscation and malicious execution behavior with repeated evidence.
